title: Armstrong's welcome in New Orleans and hearing Louis Prima
summary: A Black crowd lifted Armstrong on arrival and the band stayed at Patterson's Hotel; Randolph heard a band singing in Armstrong's manner and it was Louis Prima.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: And there's been a lot written about when the band went back to -- or, when Louis went back to New Orleans --
New Orleans, yes. I was with him at that time, when he went back.
Do you recall the reception? There's supposed to have been a great reception for Louis and --
It was. They had -- it was very good, and the last I remember seeing Louis, the crowd picked him up, and Louis was kicking -- that was comical.
Was this a black crowd, a white crowd?
All blacks, that picked him up. And I said, 'Well, we don't know where to go.' And so he said something about, go to Patterson's Hotel. Said, 'Louis, go to

Patterson's Hotel." So we went to Patterson Hotel, and finally -- that's where we found Louis, Patterson's Hotel, there on -- oh, I haven't been in New Orleans in a time. Patterson's Hotel on -- I forgot the name of the street now. Antoine or something. No, that's Detroit.
Well, anyway, did they have bands playing, some of the musicians that were down there when Louis was younger? Were they there?
I tell you who got together, I got a band -- organized a band, and someone said, there's a band down here now. See, we went to stay four weeks. I think we stayed four months. And this --
Yeah, Suburban Gardens. And they said, this band sounds just like Louis, and whenever he sings, he says, oh, you dog and everything. And Louis was singing, and come to find out it was Louis Prima.
Louis Prima, sure, yeah. Copied everything that Louis did.
